title: Cipher-Description-to-MILP Compiler
summary: The method is described as very general, but fully automating related-key differential evaluation from standard cipher descriptions remains open.

formal_statement.body: A method for evaluating cipher security with respect to related-key differential attacks is described as very general. The unresolved construction problem is whether a compiler can translate a standard cipher description, such as a hardware description language (HDL) description, into a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) instance that automates the entire related-key differential-security evaluation cycle, without assuming that HDL descriptions are already representable by the method. (S1)

scope.domain: Automated related-key differential cryptanalysis of block ciphers using mixed-integer linear programming.
assumptions: HDL descriptions are not assumed to be already representable by the method.
parameters: Standard cipher description, such as HDL: input to the proposed compiler
MILP instance: compiler output for automating the security-evaluation cycle
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a compiler can translate standard cipher descriptions into MILP instances that automate the entire related-key differential-security evaluation cycle.

citations.label: Automatic Security Evaluation and (Related-key) Differential Characteristic Search: Application to SIMON, PRESENT, LBlock, DES(L) and Other Bit-Oriented Block Ciphers

progress.summary: After describing its method as very general, the source explicitly asks whether a compiler can convert a standard cipher description, such as HDL, into an MILP instance for fully automated related-key differential-security evaluation.
